item: A redirect hop to another host reads its robots.txt and waits its interval first, a crawl kept to one site refuses a hop off it, and a redirect to an address written with a login is never followed (R629, R633)
summary: R629 (Plan's ruling on R624's independent read: "an on-site link that 302-redirects to another host is followed with no scope check and no robots.txt read for that host") and R633 (ruled on a review's measurement, folded in as its own commit). BEFORE: src/ingest/__init__.py _guarded_redirect_get re-ran the parser check and the SSRF guard on a hop and nothing else, so a page whose host answered 302 to another host was followed there with no robots.txt read and no wait for that host's interval or Crawl-delay, inside the first host's lock: a disallowing or unreadable robots.txt refused another host's pages when they were asked for and let them through when a redirect led there, and another thread could reach that host at the same moment. A crawl kept to one site (CrawlConfig.same_domain_only) followed an on-site link that redirected off the site and stored the other site's page as its own, and a sitemap on the host that redirected off it was fetched and its URLs taken. A Location that wrote a user name or password was followed: measured on 2c26ff4ac, a plain on-site link that 302s to https://alice:hunter2@good.example/landing was requested with Authorization: Basic YWxpY2U6aHVudGVyMg== and came back as the page's final and canonical URL (ingest_url stored it). NOW (R629): a page fetch carries a _RedirectChain (src/ingest/__init__.py:1026), and a hop to another host key (_host_netloc: the host and the port; the scheme alone is not another host, so an http to https upgrade on one host is unchanged) is a first request to that host (_take_hop_host, :1981): the switch is read; the chain's lock moves to the new host; its robots.txt is read (_enforce_robots, fail-closed: RobotsDisallowed or RobotsUnavailable with its cause, the same types a first request gets, the sentence ending in the fixed words "(reached by a redirect)", cached and backed off as a first read is); its interval or Crawl-delay is waited, or past the cap deferred (CrawlDelayDeferred, the next-allowed-at written first); the switch is read again (a Stop pressed during the lock wait or the interval refuses the hop). THE LOCK IS HANDED OVER, NEVER STACKED: the host left is stamped (its request was answered) and its lock released before the next lock is waited for, so a thread holds at most one host lock and two chains crossing each other (A to B on one thread, B to A on another) cannot deadlock; the hop's request and body read are under the new host's lock, so no other thread reaches that host meanwhile. A retry starts again from the first host (chain.move(chain.first)); a hop that defers on a retry reports the failed request before it, the rule the first host already had. A hop past the bound reads nothing (_MAX_REDIRECTS stays 5). The robots read (_get_robots, so declared_sitemaps too) and the two preflights pass no chain: their own hops keep today's behaviour and never read robots.txt, so a read cannot recurse. fetch(redirect_scope=) refuses a hop the scope does not cover, or cannot judge (it raises), with RedirectOutOfScope (a FetchFailed, :187) before the hop's host is looked up; crawl.py hands the site under same_domain_only (_kept_on_site, the _off_site test a harvested link takes, so a hop whose authority holds an @ is off the site too) and sitemap.py hands its host (the rule its off-host children already follow; the refused sitemap is written in errors). Both are counted as fetch_failed (classified "other"); www.good.example is the same site and another host, so its robots.txt is read before it. NOW (R633): a hop whose Location writes a userinfo (_carries_userinfo on the Location, :1941) is refused as a BlockedTarget (the type of R622's refusals of the address beside it, so a fetcher held to one host, scripts/law_pit_real_run.py, still reads it as a refused hop) in fixed words, "redirect to an address that carries a user name or password, not followed: " and the address through failure_url, after R622's parser check and before the scope, the guard and anything asked of the host, for every caller, robots reads included (a robots read that meets one is fail-closed, cause unreachable). The Location is read, not the joined URL: a relative Location writes no authority and keeps the one of the request it answers, so an address the caller wrote with a login keeps it on that host as before, and any Location that writes one is refused, the caller's own login included. TESTS: tests/test_redirect_hop_robots_r629.py, 55, through the real EthicalFetcher, crawl_source, discover_sitemap_urls, ingest_url and the preflight's _check_one over an in-memory session (every planted URL routed, so a follow is seen), a fake clock (a wait is recorded, never slept), every fetch in a bounded thread; the switch control and the R633 tests on a real requests.Session over an in-memory adapter that records every request's URL and headers. 40 fail on 2c26ff4ac (32 R629, 8 R633), the 15 controls pass (a robots read's own hop and declared_sitemaps read no robots.txt on the other host; a same-host hop, an http to https upgrade and a same-host hop to a disallowed path are unchanged; the hop past the bound; the crossing chains; an on-site hop and a www. sitemap followed; a Stop as the first host answers on a real session; the preflight ping; an @ in a path, query or fragment followed; an operator's login kept on a relative hop). On f7d064626 (R629 alone) only the 8 R633 tests fail. The three _http_get test stubs (tests/test_crawl_delay_retry_is_a_failure.py, tests/test_robots_read_refused_by_switch.py) take **_kw for the new chain keyword. RELATED: related run on cf02ee603 (232 related test files and the new file): 8,044 passed, 12 skipped, 4 failed, each failing the same way on 2c26ff4ac (tests/test_csv_feeds.py::test_feeds_api_list_and_import; tests/test_workflow_integration.py::test_full_investigative_workflow; tests/test_shared_file_writes.py::test_no_new_unlocked_write_site_and_no_stale_allowance, the same three unlocked write sites in src/ingest/__init__.py, 417, 549 and 713 on the base; tests/test_xdist_file_placement.py::test_a_real_run_announces_the_fixed_placement, pytest-xdist not installed here). A first run with R633's refusal a plain FetchFailed failed tests/test_law_pit_real_run.py's two userinfo-hop cases, which expect BlockedTarget; the refusal is a BlockedTarget now and that test is unchanged. ruff F,B clean; ruff ratchet 412; mypy clean on the three source files. Mutants, in a detached worktree, all killed: R629 18 (no robots read on the hop; no interval; the next lock taken on top of the first, killed by the crossing-chains test alone, which reports the deadlock; every caller's hop reading robots, so robots reads recurse; the crawl or the sitemap handing no scope; the scope asked after the guard and the robots read; same-host hops treated as another host; a hop deferral on a retry reported as a deferral; the host left not stamped; no switch read before or after the hop's waits; a scope that raises letting the hop through; the lock released on success only; the unrequested last hop reading robots; the "(reached by a redirect)" words dropped; the hop's host not stamped after its request; a retry not going back to the first host). R633 9 (no check; the request answered read instead of the Location; robots reads unchecked; the joined URL read, refusing an inherited login; only a changed authority refused; the address written raw; the check after the hop has taken its host; the check before R622's parser check, killed by two R622 tests whose refusal words it changes; the refusal as a plain FetchFailed). NOT CHANGED, stated: a same-host hop takes no can_fetch for its new path (the first request's decision stands; pinned as unchanged); an http to https upgrade never reads the https robots.txt; the preflight's homepage ping (src/monitoring/preflight.py:138) is made whatever robots.txt says and its hops keep today's behaviour (R633 still applies to them); a feed or sitemap page address (ingest_url) that redirects to another site is still followed, now after that host's robots.txt and interval, and stored as the source's article (only the crawl and the sitemap index are kept to one site); a hop's request rides the first host's Tor circuit as before while its robots.txt read rides the hop host's own (as any read of that host does); a transient failure at a hop is still worded against the URL asked for; a sitemap urlset's page addresses are not host-checked (ruled R626 and R627). Release-notes lines: «A page that redirects to another site is now followed only after that site's robots.txt allows it and its politeness wait has passed, and a crawl kept to one site no longer follows a redirect off it. (R629)» Proposed for R633 (Plan's line not set yet): «A page that redirects to an address written with a user name or password is no longer followed. (R633)»
